subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Localized colon and rectal cancer: staging, total neoadjuvant therapy, adjuvant chemotherapy and mismatch repair status

steps.tx: In completely resected stage III colon cancer, adjuvant fluoropyrimidine plus oxaliplatin combinations **FOLFOX** or **CAPOX** significantly reduce recurrence risk and improve overall survival. The landmark **MOSAIC trial** established that adding oxaliplatin to infusional fluorouracil achieves a durable 3-year disease-free survival benefit and a sustained 10-year overall survival advantage across resected node-positive cohorts.

left.title: FOLFOX / CAPOX
points: Statistically significant OS improvement in MOSAIC
Global standard of care for stage III disease

right.title: 5-FU / LV Monotherapy
points: Reserved for patients unfit for oxaliplatin
Inferior disease-free survival in node-positive colon

steps.tx: The international **IDEA trial** pooled data from six randomized phase III studies enrolling over 12,000 patients to evaluate adjuvant duration. In low-risk stage III colon cancer classified as **T1-3, N1**, 3 months of adjuvant CAPOX demonstrated non-inferiority to 6 months of therapy. Abbreviating therapy to 3 months dramatically reduced grade 3 or higher persistent peripheral sensory neuropathy from 16% down to 3%.

steps.tx: Universal testing for **mismatch repair deficiency** dMMR or high microsatellite instability **MSI-H** provides vital prognostic and predictive stratification in stage II colon cancer. Patients harbouring dMMR tumours demonstrate a superior natural prognosis with lower baseline recurrence rates. However, retrospective analyses confirm that dMMR stage II tumours derive no therapeutic benefit from single-agent fluoropyrimidine adjuvant chemotherapy, justifying clinical observation alone.

steps.tx: In mismatch repair-proficient stage II colon cancer, adjuvant chemotherapy decisions depend strictly upon high-risk clinicopathological features. Key high-risk indicators encompass **T4 primary tumour** invading visceral peritoneum, presentation with acute bowel obstruction or perforation, poorly differentiated histology, prominent lymphovascular or perineural invasion, and inadequate surgical lymph node evaluation examining **fewer than 12 sampled lymph nodes**.

steps.tx: Modern multimodal management of locally advanced rectal cancer utilizes **Total neoadjuvant therapy** TNT. In the landmark phase III **RAPIDO trial**, delivering short-course radiotherapy 5 x 5 Gy followed by consolidation CAPOX or FOLFOX prior to total mesorectal excision significantly halved disease-related treatment failure and reduced distant metastases compared with standard preoperative chemoradiotherapy.

steps.tx: Both MRI views show a bulky **rectal tumour** breaching the wall with **extramural spread** into fat. The outline traces the **mesorectal fascia** and the planned radiotherapy field around it. This anatomy explains **Total neoadjuvant therapy** where short course radiation plus consolidation chemotherapy comes before surgery to cut distant failure.
steps.say: The two MRI views show the rectal tumour pushing through the wall into nearby fat with the fascia and radiation field drawn around it. When disease looks like this, care starts with short course radiation and consolidation chemotherapy before removal of the rectum and its fatty envelope. That order lowers distant spread and treatment failure.

steps.tx: Complementing the consolidation strategy, the phase III **PRODIGE 23** trial evaluated induction chemotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer. Administering neoadjuvant modified **mFOLFIRINOX** for 6 cycles prior to concurrent chemoradiotherapy and total mesorectal excision produced significantly higher pathological complete response rates and prolonged 7-year overall survival and disease-free survival over standard preoperative chemoradiation alone.

right.title: Standard Preoperative CRT
points: Immediate surgery followed by adjuvant therapy

steps.tx: In mismatch repair-deficient locally advanced rectal cancer, single-agent PD-1 inhibitor **Dostarlimab** monotherapy for 6 months achieved a historic clinical breakthrough. In a prospective phase II study, neoadjuvant dostarlimab produced an unprecedented **100% clinical complete response rate** across all treated patients, completely avoiding surgical resection, pelvic radiation therapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy while preserving rectal organ function.

steps.tx: A non-operative **Watch-and-wait** organ preservation strategy is now an evidence-based management pathway for rectal cancer patients achieving a confirmed **clinical complete response** following total neoadjuvant therapy. Rigorous surveillance requires digital rectal examination, flexible sigmoidoscopy, and high-resolution pelvic MRI every 3 to 4 months for 2 years, with prompt surgical salvage if endoluminal tumour regrowth occurs.

rows: Complete normalisation of rectal wall palpation
White scar, telangiectasias; no residual ulcer or nodule
Dark T2 scar (mrTRG 1); no residual nodal enlargement
Surveillance for occult systemic distant metastases

steps.tx: The pelvic MRI shows a smooth dark **fibrotic scar** replacing the former rectal tumor after total neoadjuvant therapy. The surrounding fatty **mesorectum** looks intact with no residual mass or enlarged nodes. This appearance matches a **clinical complete response** graded mrTRG 1. Such patients may enter a watch and wait path with close scopes and scans instead of immediate surgery.
steps.say: The axial rectal MRI shows only a thin dark scar where the cancer had been, with no visible remaining tumor and no swollen nodes in the nearby mesorectum. The fatty envelope around the rectum is preserved and clean. This is the imaging definition of a complete response after upfront chemoradiation plus chemotherapy. When exams and scopes agree, the patient can be watched closely with regular rectal exams, scopes and MRI, keeping surgery in reserve if regrowth appears.

vis.alt: The pelvic MRI shows a dark rectal wall scar with an intact mesorectum and no residual tumor.
vis.caption: Post therapy MRI shows complete rectal response with scarring. Illustration: StewardMD original.
